name: squad-ux-stakeholder-empathy
description: "Use empathy beyond users to understand evidenced collaborator and stakeholder constraints, expose trade-offs, and coordinate respectful UX decisions without assuming motives or overriding authority."
---

# Empathy Beyond Users

## Procedure
1. Identify the authorized design decision and affected collaborators, operators, support teams, and stakeholders. Use approved product-owned records and avoid unnecessary personal data.
2. Ask through permitted channels about priorities, business risks, technical difficulty, support burden, and accessibility constraints. For Squad-led work, use the accepted collaboration/Factory handoff rather than assuming direct stakeholder or VOC delegation is available. Do not infer stress, emotion, or intent without evidence.
3. Separate stated constraints, observed facts, preferences, and assumptions. Surface conflicts between user benefit and downstream burden.
4. Present feasible alternatives with consequences and decision ownership. ProductOwner decides priority, technical owners assess feasibility, and the human approves consequential commitments.
5. Record accepted responsibilities, dissent, and next actions. Verify the handoff actually addresses constraints rather than claiming consensus or mutual understanding by assertion.

## Completion Checks
Trade-offs and affected parties are visible, respectful, and evidence-linked. No unauthorized stakeholder contact, false empathy claims, hidden pressure, or role-boundary override.

Original procedure informed by item 20 of [UX Playbook's UX skills article](https://uxplaybook.org/articles/top-skills-every-ux-designer-needs), accessed October 11, 2026.
